With Corin the equality moved a third time and was not named: on Day 171, while Jorra’s bent finger stood in the cold damper and Sella’s instruction was allowed to finish, his broom checked half a beat behind the standing finger on the flagstones and went on without a word or a turn of the head, the Seed 22 half-check returned changed after a hundred and fifty days, held and unspoken and no mercy. With Jorra the old shape held under one roof, neither asking about the other’s silence; the wheel-keeper gave no name to the men who went into the back room and Tarn gave no word to the fraction at the iron. On Day 172 at the kindling he told the wood \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count}, six counted in the worn thumb-mark where the house can check and the seventh held at the lip where it cannot, the small knife at the very edge with Garl’s unforged collector sentence beside it, and brought the ear-sentence to his teeth and no further; he drew the breath he should have spent, did not call the loan, stood no tenth before the seventh year was earned, and the loan stayed uncalled. No bond paid or spoken, no new scar or possession.

\textbf{Ch 42 (bonds).} With Sella nothing changed: he takes the broom only after it has been given its instruction, calls her house, and she has not asked about his seventh year or his ear. With Corin the equality held through the last tend without a word: two ears, two silences, a loan that can hear and has never been called. With Jorra the old shape held under one roof — the wheel-keeper’s dust and waiting finger, the debt’s stroke going on over the flagstones past the bright patch without the half-check — neither man naming the other’s silence and the Day 171 movement not repeated as a new change. The warm stone stays cold in the pot in the loft, unreconciled by not trying, which is not forgiving. No bond paid or spoken, no new scar or possession.

\textbf{Ch 43 (bonds).} With Sella nothing changed: he takes the broom only after she has given it its instruction, calls her \emph{house}, agrees with the early thaw and the late while keeping the late because it puts off the paying, and she has not asked about his seventh year or his ear. With Corin the equality held through Ember 1–3 without a word: two ears, two silences, a loan that can hear and has never been called; the boy’s turning toward the early note of a pot set down wrong was seen by the woman who set it down and not by her, and Tarn did not turn or name the sound. With Jorra the old shape held under one roof, neither asking about the back room or the ear: Jorra’s dust came out of the room before first grey on Days 181 and 182, his knowing of the pot’s full note stayed on the near-full tray with no pot lost, and his bent finger stood in the cold damper until Sella’s sentence was finished, while Tarn’s stroke went on over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch without the half-check. Garl’s unforged collector sentence stayed beside the knife with six counted where the house can check and the seventh held where it cannot, the Seed 16 breath unspent, nine stoppings still nine objects with no tenth and the loan uncalled. The warm stone in the clay pot in the loft stays cold and unreconciled by not trying, which is not forgiving. No bond paid or spoken, no new scar or possession, no change of voice.

\textbf{Ch 44 (bonds).} With Sella nothing changed: he takes the broom only after she has given it its instruction, calls her \emph{house}, says \emph{Yes, house} to an early thaw and a late while keeping the late because it puts off the paying, and she has not asked about his seventh year or his ear. With Corin the equality held through Ember 4–6 without a word: two ears, two silences, a loan that can hear and has never been called. \textbf{His one act of the chapter is a movement of the keeping he holds for Sella:} on the afternoon of Day 183 he goes up to the Debt Loft and takes the warm stone she gave him in the winter Garl died out of the clay pot with no mark on it, two years gone and cold and not looked at in a year; he holds it, sets it on the sill where light comes through the finger’s-width opening, looks at it a long moment and puts it back. No word, no figure, no payer, no slate. He does not reconcile the stone with the debt and does not forgive it, for not trying is not forgiving, and the debt stands exactly as it stood; the stone lies back in its pot, cold, and he moves on with the broom (T006 advanced, T036/T076 advanced, not paid). With Jorra the old shape held under one roof on Days 184 and 185: the wheel-keeper’s dust and his bent finger standing in the cold damper while the debt’s stroke went on over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch without the half-check, neither man naming the other’s silence, and the finger in the iron a remembered holding and not a new change. The ear-sentence stopped short of the word that would call the loan on all three days, no tenth stood up before the seventh year was earned, the Seed 16 breath stayed unspent and the loan stayed uncalled. No bond paid or spoken, no new scar or possession, no change of voice.

\textbf{Ch 45 (bonds).} With Sella nothing changed: he takes the broom only after it has been given its instruction, calls her \emph{house}, says \emph{Yes, house} to an early thaw and a late while keeping the late because it puts off the paying, and she has not asked about his seventh year or his ear. With Corin the equality held through Ember 7–9 at the place it had moved to — two ears, two silences, a loan that can hear and has never been called — and the boy’s filing of the carried body’s pale line as a danger worth nothing was not a hearing joined to his own held breath. With Jorra the old shape held under one roof, neither asking about the back room or the ear: three or four men unnamed went low into the finger’s-width-open back room before first grey on Day 187, Jorra’s dust was ground small as meal past the bent finger, and his bent finger stood in the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence while the debt’s stroke went on over the flagstones without the half-check, the two silences unjoined and the loan uncalled. Garl’s unforged collector sentence stayed beside the knife at the edge of its sill; Mira’s noticing and his answered weather were unchanged. No bond was paid, sold or spoken, and no new scar or possession came; the warm stone in its unmarked pot in the loft stayed cold and unreconciled by not trying, which is not forgiving (T006 held).

\textbf{Ch 46 (bonds).} With Sella nothing changed: he takes the broom only after it has been instructed, calls her \emph{house}, says \emph{Yes, house} to an early thaw and a late while keeping the late because it puts off the paying, sweeps the collector’s road without turning and no collector comes, and she has not asked about his seventh year or his ear. With Corin the equality held through Ember 10–12 at the place it had moved to — two ears, two silences, a loan that can hear and has never been called — and the boy’s filing of Berr’s read figure beside the paid figure was not a hearing joined to his own held breath. With Jorra the old shape held under one roof, neither asking about the back room or the ear: men unnamed went low into the back room before first grey on Days 190 and 191, Jorra’s dust was ground small as meal past the bent finger, and his bent finger stood in the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence as a remembered holding and not a new change while Tarn’s stroke went on over the flagstones without the half-check. The small knife lay at the edge of its sill with six counted where the house can check and the seventh at the lip where it cannot, Garl’s unforged collector sentence beside it; the Seed 16 breath stayed unspent, the ear-sentence came to the threshold of the word on all three days and stopped, nine stoppings stayed nine with no tenth before the seventh year was earned, and the loan stayed uncalled. The warm stone lay cold and unreconciled in its pot in the loft. No bond was paid, sold or spoken, no new scar or possession came, and the seventh year had still not given.

\CRsheetheading{Arc So Far}
He enters already sweeping, before anyone wakes, a bent man of twenty-two with grey Ash in the creases of his knuckles and a pale ring round his left wrist where the clip sat in Y.H. 806. Six years of a seven-year term lie behind him and he has counted every one and will not count the next. In Chapter 2 he pockets the small bench knife and then says of his own accord that he took it and put it back and they can check; he stops his broom for two strokes when a pot is set down and gives its flat note, turns his head a degree and says nothing; he banks the coals without looking at the fire. When the foundling is given a bed and he is given the loft he makes one short sentence of it and goes back to sweeping. His deference has a nail in it, and the nail is the one possession the house cannot check.

On Days 5 and 6 he sweeps twice and says nothing. The small knife goes into his pocket and back onto the sill where it can be checked, announced unasked both times; the broom stops for two strokes when a Vail pot gives its flat note through the wall, and he does not turn his head or name the sound. The reader sees the second ear in the house; nobody under the roof does. Six years of seven are behind him and he will not count the seventh, which is the one entry in the house the house cannot check. He keeps his head down over the broom and the one thing he owns out of the house’s reach.

On Days 7, 8 and 9 the ear is no longer only the reader’s. He sees the boy expect a note from a pot that has not yet been set down, and stops his own broom at the set-down that gives nothing, and the two of them go on under one roof without a word between them --- a loan that can hear now knowing he is not the only one, which makes the thing he owns both more valuable and more dangerous. The small knife goes back to its sill and is announced unasked; six of seven years are counted and the seventh is held back, the one entry in the house the house cannot check. He stops for two breaths when Sella says he has done well and then goes on sweeping, because an argument has nowhere to put its foot when a man agrees with everything.

On Days 10 through 14 the seventh year stays held back and the ear stays kept from the other side of the same silence. He measures the kindling as a debt and finds a fifth place empty; the knife goes to its sill and is announced twice more; when Sella tells him he has done well the broom stops for two breaths, the nearest thing this house allows to being struck by a kindness he cannot enter. A pot turned toward on the bench gives nothing and his broom checks half a stroke at the empty set-down, a second silent keeping beside the boy’s. He holds the pale clip-ring to the light and says the breath takes a man in his sleep and that Mud End called such a death merciful, and wants the thaw late because a late thaw puts off what is payable. The ear is worth more than the debt that holds him, which makes it dangerous, and he has said nothing of it to anyone.

On Days 15 through 24 the seventh year stays held back and the ear is exercised twice without being spoken. He goes for a collector for a neighbour and brings back a man with grey fingertips, and on the way a carried vessel gives its flat note past the door; his head turns a degree, his hand goes back to the broom, and only the boy under the roof sees the turn. A pot cracks in the yard two paces from the basket and his broom checks at the place where it stood and goes on. The knife goes to its sill and is announced to the empty yard on Stone 22, 23 and 30; on Stone 29 he offers to check the Ash ridge by thumb, the nearest a clay-bound hand comes to touching what the house keeps out of its accounts. He still wants his exact account and grudges the house the loan of a bed; a loan that can hear is a loan that can be called, and the sentence has never been said in the house where it is truest.

On Days 25 through 30 the seventh year stays held back and the ear stays kept from the other side of the same silence. The knife goes to its sill and is announced unasked to the empty yard, six of seven years are counted every day and the seventh is never named; the Ash in his knuckles is the colour of the ridge nobody will sweep and no scrubbing lifts it. In the Long Night he says the six and holds the seventh back in the dark, and sets the knife where it can be checked; the boy hears the told bell beside the heard bell and he says nothing about either. He still wants the thaw late because it puts off the paying, and on Ilmen 1, with the Ash burned and called dealt with and the district’s slates opened elsewhere, he sweeps toward the slip pits with the count unchanged. The loan that can hear is a loan that can be called, and the sentence has still never been said in the house where it is truest.

On Days 31 through 37 the seventh year stays held back and the ear stays kept from the other side of the same silence. The small knife goes to its sill and is announced unasked; six of seven years are counted every day and the seventh is never named; the Ash in his knuckles is the colour of the burned ridge’s old place, which is now a clean dark line. He wants the thaw late because a late thaw puts off the paying, and the thaw is coming on anyway. On Ilmen 6 his head turns a degree at the nearly-full note in open light and he says nothing, and the boy hears it and says nothing, so two not-sayings stand in the same place. The loan that can hear is a loan that can be called, and the sentence has still never been said in the house where it is truest.

On Days 38 through 44 the seventh year stays held back and the ear stays kept from the other side of the same silence. The small knife is on its sill before light on the first morning and back on it at dusk, announced to the empty yard, six years counted and the seventh held back; Ash is worked into the knuckles that no scrubbing lifts. He swept the place by the bench where no note had come, swept around the corner where the clay-heavy water had come up behind the racks, and swept the road toward the Fishstairs over and over without turning, the road a man goes down when a house wants a collector; no collector came for the woman in the brook and he did not go for one. On Ilmen 11 he set the knife on its sill, told the yard \emph{It’s back. You can check}, held the seventh year back and wanted the late thaw because a late thaw puts off the paying. He agreed with both sides about the water and said nothing about the omission or the sound the yard had not heard. On Ilmen 15 the knife was back on its sill and the count unchanged, and he did not look toward the bed where the boy lay with both crusts in the fold.

On Days 45 through 47 the seventh year stays held back and the ear stays kept from the other side of the same silence. The small knife is on its sill before the light goes, announced to the empty yard on the first two mornings and to nobody on the third, because the yard has already been told; Ash is worked into the knuckles that no scrubbing lifts and the pale clip-ring holds the light and gives it back. His broom goes over the road to the Fishstairs without once looking along it, and no collector comes down it for the woman the brook took nine mornings ago, and he does not say that the thing which has not happened has a name. He agrees with the early thaw and the late and keeps wanting the late one because it puts off the paying. When Sella tells him he has done well he stops for two breaths and then goes on. The boy keeps Tarn’s silence beside his own and does not let the two touch; a loan that can hear is a loan that can be called, and the sentence has still never been said in the house where it is truest.

On Days 48 through 54 the seventh year stays held back and the ear stays kept from the other side of the same silence. The small knife lies on its sill with six counted and the seventh never named; Ash is worked into the knuckles that no scrubbing lifts and the pale clip-ring holds the light and gives it back. His eye goes a degree toward the slack oiled paper before the light does and he says nothing. A vessel gives its note past the yard door on Day 50 and another pot answers nearly full on Day 52, and his head does not turn at either and he does not call either a seventh hearing or name the sound in Grathic. He agrees with the ones who want the thaw early and the ones who want it late and keeps wanting the late one because a late thaw puts off the paying; his broom goes over the collector’s road on Days 50 and 53 without once turning along it and no collector goes down it for the woman the brook took. He does not look toward the bed or the basket. A loan that can hear is a loan that can be called, and the sentence has still never been said in the house where it is truest.

On Days 55 through 60 the seventh year stays held back and the ear stays kept from the other side of the same silence. The small knife is on its sill the whole time with six counted and the seventh never named, the one entry in this house the house cannot check; Ash is worked into the knuckles in the colour of the clean dark line and the pale clip-ring holds the light and gives it back. At the well and in the yard he agrees with the early thaw and the late, saying \emph{Yes, house} to each, and keeps wanting the late one because a late thaw puts off the paying. His broom goes over the road to the Fishstairs over and over without once turning along it, and no collector comes down it for the woman the brook took; the omission has no word and has not made a doctrine of itself. On Ilmen 28 a vessel gives its flat note past the yard door and his head does not turn and he does not name the sound; two ears keep their equality under one roof and the loan that can hear stays uncalled. When Sella tells him he has done well he stops altogether for two breaths, then sets the knife where it can be checked and goes back to the broom. On Silt 1 he keeps sweeping toward the thaw while the month turns and the brook runs higher; the count is unchanged. A loan that can hear is a loan that can be called, and the sentence has still never been said in the house where it is truest.

On Days 61 through 67 the seventh year presses against the rising water and is still held back. The small knife lies on its sill and is announced to the empty yard, six counted and the seventh nearly gone but never named; Ash is worked into the knuckles in the colour of the clean dark line and the pale clip-ring holds the light and gives it back. He agrees with the early thaw and the late so thoroughly that there is nowhere for an argument to put its foot, and keeps wanting the late one because it puts off the paying, though the brook is higher and the paying comes with the water. His broom checks half a stroke at the cracked-pot place and goes on, and his head does not turn at a vessel’s note past the door; on Silt 6 it goes a degree toward a nearly-full pot and back to the broom. He does not name either sound or look toward the basket. Jorra’s dust out of the back room goes unremarked by him, and he does not look at the dusty forearms. Two ears keep their equality under one roof and the loan that can hear stays uncalled; the sentence that would call it lies under the days as it has lain for six years. A loan that can hear is a loan that can be called, and it has still never been said in the house where it is truest.

On Days 68 through 74 the seventh year presses against the flood and is still held back. The knife goes to its sill and is announced to the empty yard, six counted and the seventh nearly gone and never named; Ash is worked into the knuckles in the colour of the clean dark line and the pale clip-ring holds what light there is and gives it back. He agrees with the early thaw and the late so entirely that no argument can find a foot and keeps wanting the late one because it puts off the paying, though the paying has come up the road and stands in the hollows of the bank. His broom goes over the road a house sends a man down when it wants a collector without once turning along it, and when a vessel gives its note past the door in the afternoon of Silt 15 his head does not turn and he does not name the sound. Two ears keep their equality under one roof and the loan that can hear stays uncalled; the sentence that would call it lies under the days as it has for six years. A loan that can hear is a loan that can be called, and it has still never been said in the house where it is truest.

On Days 75 through 77 the seventh year stands at the edge of the sill and is held. The knife is where it can be checked and the seventh is where it cannot; the broom goes over the collector’s road without turning and a whole vessel gives its note past the door without a turn of the head. The boy has brought a new shape into the yard --- a head that turns a half-beat after the knock, a loaf that passes without a slate --- and Tarn does not turn toward that either, and the boy does not put the two turnings together. The equality under the roof is unchanged: two ears, two silences, an ear worth more than a debt, and a loan that can hear and has never been called. Something must give at the end of the seventh year, and the end was not written here.

On Days 78 through 84 the seventh year stands at the edge of the sill and is held. The lean week goes around the mud the flood left and Tarn goes around it with the same broom and the same account: six years standing in a mark his thumb has worn almost flat, the seventh nearly gone and still held back, announced to the empty yard before the light and not named to the kindling except as the one he does not count. Ash in his knuckles is the colour of the clean dark line the yard will not sweep and no scrubbing lifts it; the clip-ring at his wrist holds the little light. He agrees so completely with the early thaw and the late that an argument has nowhere to put its foot, and wants the late because it puts off the paying, though the paying stands in the ruts. His broom goes over the collector’s road over and over without a turn. When a vessel gives its note past the door he does not turn and does not name it, and the boy does not call it a seventh hearing; two ears and two silences keep their equality under one roof. The head that turns half a beat late at the well is not his and he does not join it to anything. Something must give at the end of the seventh year, and the end was not written here; the loan that can hear stays uncalled.

On Days 85 through 90 the seventh year stands at the edge of the sill through the turn of Silt into Seed and is still held. The small bench knife is on its sill before the light on Silt 26, 27 and Seed 1; he tells the sill first and the yard after where it is, six years standing in a mark his thumb has worn almost flat and the seventh never cut, nearly gone and still held, the one entry in this house the house cannot check. To the kindling he says \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count.} Ash is worked into the creases of his knuckles in the colour of the clean dark line and no scrubbing lifts it; the pale clip-ring at his left wrist holds what light there is and gives it back. He says \emph{Yes, house} to both sides of the thaw argument, agrees so entirely that no argument can find a foot, and keeps wanting the late because it puts off the paying, though the paying has stood in the ruts all week and goes over the boundary into Seed unchanged. His broom goes over the road a house sends a man down when it wants a collector, over and over, without once turning along it, and no collector comes. He has been sent for one once, in the Long Cold, and come back at the frozen ford and told the house it had been done; he keeps that sentence where he keeps the seventh year and neither is entered. A vessel gives its note past the door on Silt 27 and again on Seed 1 and his head does not turn and he does not name the sound; the boy does not call either a seventh hearing. He takes the broom from Sella’s hands on Seed 1 only after she has given it its instruction, and the first work of the planting month is sweeping. Two ears and two silences keep their equality under one roof; the loan that can hear stays uncalled. Something must give at the end of the seventh year; it did not give here, and the count crosses into Seed with the seventh still held.

He says \emph{Yes, house} to the early thaw and the late, agrees so entirely no argument can find a foot, and keeps wanting the late because it puts off the paying, though the paying has stood in the ruts since the water went. Something must give at the end of the seventh year; it did not give here.

His chest is tight and there is a small interval at the top of each reach where the breath should have gone in. \textbf{On Seed 22, for the first time, the equality under the roof moves:} while Jorra’s bent finger stands in the cold damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence, Tarn’s stroke checks for half a beat on the flagstones and then goes on toward the road without a word or a turn of the head, the flagstones keeping the place where the stroke stopped as a thing nobody would enter. Neither man names the other’s silence and the loan that can hear is not called; the boy sets the half-check beside the bent finger on one tray and lays no finger across them. Two ears and two silences still keep their equality under one roof, the ear worth more than the debt and therefore unsafe. He keeps the sentence from the frozen ford where he keeps the seventh year and enters neither. Something must give at the end of the seventh year; it did not give here, and the breath presses to its edge into Chapter 25.

On Days 126 through 128 the seventh year is pressed further past its third tend and still held, and the thing that must give at its end has not given. Under the wheel-shed Jorra’s bent finger leads at the damper ahead of an unfinished sentence and the dust comes out of the back room from men unnamed; Tarn’s stroke goes on over the flagstones without the half-check while the stones keep the shallow bright patch where it stopped, neither man naming the other’s silence. Three stoppings now stand on the interval tray and none of them is a payment. Through Days 183–185 (Ember 4–6) the seventh year stands nearer its end than it has ever stood and has still not given. The small knife lies at the very edge of its sill with six counted in the worn thumb-mark where the house can check and the seventh held at the lip where it cannot, Garl’s unforged collector sentence beside it and the Seed 16 breath unspent with its small interval at the top of each reach; Ash is worked into the creases of his knuckles in the colour of the clean dark line and no scrubbing lifts it, the pale clip-ring at his left wrist holds what light there is and gives it back, and his chest has been tight since the dark. He takes the broom only after it has been given its instruction, says \emph{Yes, house} to an early thaw and a late, agrees so entirely that no argument finds a foot and goes on wanting the late one because it puts off the paying; his broom goes over the road a house sends a man down when it wants a collector, without once turning along it, and no collector comes. On all three days he tells the kindling \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count} and brings the ear-sentence to his teeth and no further: he draws the breath he should have spent, does not say the word that would call the loan, stands no tenth stopping up to join the nine because the seventh year has not yet been earned, and the loan stays uncalled. His stroke goes on over the shallow bright patch on the flagstones without the half-check, so the Day 171 movement stays a held change on its own place beside the Day 161 damper fraction and the Day 166 shelf beat, not repeated as a new change and not paired into a rule with a payer. \textbf{His change in the chapter is a movement of a keeping, not a settlement:} on the afternoon of Day 183 he goes up into the Debt Loft and takes the warm stone Sella gave him in the winter Garl died out of the clay pot with no mark on it where it has lain two years gone and cold, not looked at in a year. He holds it in both hands, turns it so the light from the finger’s-width opening finds the smooth place on one face, sets it on the sill where a man coming up the ladder would see it, stands over it a long while, then puts it back in the pot and sets the pot’s foot down where it had stood. No word, no figure, no payer, no slate; he does not reconcile the stone with the debt and does not forgive it, for not trying is not forgiving, and the debt stands exactly as it stood. The stone lies back in the pot, cold and unreconciled, and on the two following days he files the remembering as a remembering and not a holding made again. Jorra’s bent finger stands in the cold damper on Days 184 and 185 until Sella’s sentence reaches the pot, and on both days the fraction is a remembered holding and not a new change; neither man asks about the ear or the room and the two silences stay unjoined. He gives no name to the men who go into the back room before first grey. He is a debt with hands who has looked once at what was given and put it back, and nothing in the house has moved toward a payment.

Through Days 186–188 (Ember 7–9) the seventh year stands nearer its end than it has ever stood and has still not given. The small knife lies at the very edge of its sill with six counted in the worn thumb-mark where the house can check and the seventh held at the lip where it cannot, Garl’s unforged collector sentence beside it, the Seed 16 breath unspent with its small interval at the top of each reach, his chest tight since the dark, Ash worked into the knuckle creases in the colour of the clean dark line, the pale clip-ring at the left wrist holding what light there is. He takes the broom only after it has been instructed, says \emph{Yes, house} to an early thaw and a late, agrees so entirely that no argument can find a foot and keeps wanting the late because it puts off the paying; his broom goes over the collector’s road without once turning along it and no collector comes (T036/T076). On all three days he told the kindling \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count} and brought the sentence about an ear under this roof being worth more than the debt that holds it all the way to the word that would call the loan, with no figure and no name; he drew the breath he should have spent and did not spend it, stood no tenth stopping up to join the nine because the seventh year has not yet been earned, and the loan stayed uncalled (T036/T076, T061/T082). His stroke went on over the shallow bright patch on the flagstones without the half-check, so the Day 171 movement stayed a held change on its own place beside the Day 161 damper fraction and the Day 166 shelf beat, not repeated as a new change and not paired into a rule (T062, T100). Jorra’s men went unnamed into the back room before first grey on Day 187 and he did not ask about the room while Jorra did not ask about the ear; the two silences stayed unjoined (T035/T031). He was at the edge of the work on Day 188 when a rack-worker’s pot sang itself out early and two men carried a glaze-room hand out across the yard toward the clay road, and he went on with his broom and gave no name to what ailed the man; the boy was the only adult in the yard and the least use in it, and the two ears kept their silence around a cost entered nowhere (T077 advanced, not paid). The warm stone Sella gave him in the winter Garl died lay back in its unmarked clay pot in the loft, two years gone and cold, unreconciled by not trying, which is not forgiving; from below the boy filed the remembered holding as a remembering and not a holding made again, on a fourth place of its own with no fourth likeness stood up as a cause (T006 held, T061/T082). Something must give at the end of the seventh year and it did not give here.

On Days 189 through 191 his seventh year stands nearer its end than it has ever stood and still holds: six counted in the worn thumb-mark where the house can check and the seventh at the lip where it cannot, the small knife at the edge of its sill with Garl’s unforged collector sentence beside it, the Seed 16 breath unspent and nine stoppings still nine objects with no tenth before the seventh year is earned. He takes the broom only after it is instructed, says \emph{Yes, house} to an early thaw and a late while wanting the late because it puts off the paying, sweeps the collector’s road without turning and no collector comes. The ear-sentence comes to the threshold of the word that would call the loan on all three days and stops there with no figure and no name, and the loan stays uncalled. His stroke goes over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch without the half-check, and the warm stone lies cold and unreconciled in its pot in the loft. No bond paid or spoken; nothing has given.

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 1: Does not appear; the broom, the knife and the loft are held for Chapter 2.

\item Ch 2: Swept the kiln-house before anyone woke and stopped for two strokes at a pot’s flat note without turning his head or naming the sound. Put the small bench knife in his pocket, then took it out and put it back where it could be checked and said so unasked. Told Sella \emph{Six years. One to go. I’ve counted every one, and I won’t count the next.} Carried up from the Debt Loft with a broom on the third day, banked the coals, and said \emph{He’s a foundling. I’m a debt. Don’t put us in the same sentence, Sella.} when the boy was given a bed. Heard the second flat note of the three days from a pot set down on the bench and did not say what it was.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 4: Days 5 and 6. Swept before light on Stone 11 and again at dusk on Stone 12, with Ash in his knuckles and the pale ring at his left wrist. Took the small bench knife out and put it back where it could be checked, saying so unasked both times. His broom stopped for two strokes at the flat note of a pot through the shed wall and he did not turn his head, name the sound or say that it was a sound at all --- the second ear in the house, witnessed only by the reader. Said \emph{yes, house; I’ll sweep it; I swept it this morning; I’ll sweep it again} to the ground and kept his head down over the broom. Six of seven years counted, the seventh not counted. He said nothing about the note all day, and nobody asked him to.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 5: Days 7--9. On Stone 13 came up the yard with the small knife already back on its sill, checked it with his eyes only, and saw the boy turn his head toward a pot before Jorra set it down; his broom stopped half a stroke at the set-down that gave nothing and he said nothing about either. Counted six years of seven and held the seventh back, and stopped altogether for two breaths when Sella said he had done well, then swept again. At dusk put the knife back where it could be checked and announced it unasked, and kept his head down over the broom while Sella counted loaves and bits. Said nothing all three days about the note that did not come, and nobody asked him to.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

The next I don’t count.} On Stone 17 set the small knife on its sill and told the yard to check, stopped altogether for two breaths when Sella said \emph{you’ve done well} and said \emph{Yes, house} before going on; his broom checked half a stroke when a pot turned toward on the bench gave nothing. Scraped Ash from his knuckles with the knife, held the pale ring at his left wrist up to the light and put the knife back without announcing it this time. Named the kiln’s breath as the danger and said a man in Mud End who slept before a kiln with the damper shut was called a merciful death; said he would take the late thaw, a longer week before the paying. On Stone 18 said he had swept and would sweep again; on Stone 19 agreed a late thaw was a longer week before the paying and offered to check the ridge; on Stone 20, Account-day, told the yard again the knife was back on its sill and let his broom stop half a stroke at the place where no note had come. Six of seven years counted all five days, the seventh held back and never named.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

You can check}, and said to the kindling \emph{Six counted; the next I don’t count}; was sent for a collector for a neighbour two doors down and returned with a man whose cuff was soft from washing and fingertips the colour of skimmed milk gone off, who said \emph{the measure is taken and the account stands as entered} to a slate. On the way back his head turned a degree at a vessel’s flat note carried past the door and he did not name it or look at the basket. On Stone 29 held the pale clip-ring at his left wrist to the light, said \emph{I can check the width, house. I’ve a thumb as good as any}, and took his eyes off the ridge. On Stone 30 the knife was back on its sill and announced once more, unasked. Six of the seven years counted every day, the seventh held back and never named; the ear kept silent and the loan uncalled.

The next I don’t count} and the yard \emph{I owe six}, and his chest was tight with the breath still unspent. Ash was worked into the creases of his knuckles in the colour of the clean dark line and no scrubbing lifted it; the pale clip-ring at his left wrist held what light there was and gave it back. He called everyone \emph{house}, said \emph{Yes, house} to those who wanted the thaw early and those who wanted it late, agreed so entirely that no argument could find a foot and kept wanting the late because it puts off the paying, though the paying had stood in the ruts since the water went. He took the broom only after Sella had given it its instruction and swept the collector’s road over and over without once turning along it, keeping the unforged sentence from the frozen ford where he keeps the seventh year and entering neither; no collector came. On Seed 19 he was in the yard and the shed while men unnamed came before first grey, and he did not turn or speak when Jorra’s bent finger went into the damper ahead of Sella’s unfinished sentence. The two ears kept their equality and the loan stayed uncalled; something must give at the end of the seventh year and it did not give here, the breath pressed to its edge. Offstage on Seed 20. No new scar, possession or change of voice.

The next I don’t count}, brought the ear-sentence to his teeth and no further with no figure and no name, drew the breath he did not spend, and left the loan uncalled with nine stoppings still nine and no tenth (T061/T082). When Jorra’s bent finger waited at the damper on Day 161 until Sella had finished her sentence he said nothing of the fraction, and neither man named the other’s silence. The warm stone Sella gave him in the winter Garl died is still in his clay pot in the loft, cold and unreconciled with the debt, and he has stopped trying, which is not forgiving (T006 held). No new scar or possession, no bond paid or spoken.

\end{itemize}

\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=1.4em,itemsep=1pt,topsep=3pt,parsep=0pt]

\item Ch 40: Days 163, 164, 165, 166 and 168, on stage under the Vail roof, at the kindling, the damper, the flagstones and in the yard; offstage on the Weir day and the Account-day. Took the broom only after it was instructed and said \emph{Yes, house} to an early thaw and a late, going on wanting the late because it puts off the paying (T036/T076). Seventh year nearer its end than it has ever stood and still held: six counted where the house can check and the seventh at the lip of the sill where it cannot, the small knife at the very edge with Garl’s unforged collector sentence beside it, Seed 16 breath unspent, chest tight since the dark, Ash worked into the knuckle creases in the colour of the clean dark line and the pale clip-ring at the left wrist holding what light there is. Stroke over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch without the half-check and over the collector’s road without turning along it; no collector came. On Day 164, when Sella’s instruction to the fire went low, Jorra’s bent finger went to the cold damper and waited for the sentence to finish; he took the broom and said nothing of the fraction (T062), and neither man named the other’s silence. On Day 165, with the coals banked and the knife at the edge of its sill, told the kindling \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count} and brought the ear-sentence all the way to the word that would call the loan, with no figure and no name; he stopped there, drew the breath he did not spend, said \emph{Yes, house} to the fire and went on with the broom. Nine stoppings remained nine objects with no payer named to any, no tenth stood up before the seventh year was earned, the loan stayed uncalled and no collector came (T036/T076, T061/T082). A kiln-hand’s sideways word about the man in Mud End taken quiet in his sleep was called merciful and made into no lesson. The warm stone Sella gave him in the winter Garl died still lies in the clay pot in the loft, cold and unreconciled with the debt, and he has stopped trying, which is not forgiving (T006 held). No new scar or possession, no bond paid or spoken.

\item Ch 41: Days 170, 171 and 172, Tallow 21–23, on stage at the kindling, the flagstones, the damper and the Clay Yard. Took the broom only after it had been instructed and said \emph{Yes, house} to an early thaw and a late, going on wanting the late because it puts off the paying though the paying had stood in the ruts since the water went; his broom went over the collector’s road without once turning along it and no collector came (T036/T076). Seventh year nearer its end than it has ever stood and still held: six counted in the worn thumb-mark where the house can check, the seventh at the lip of the sill where it cannot, the small knife at the very edge with Garl’s unforged collector sentence beside it, the Seed 16 breath unspent with its interval at the top of each reach, his chest tight since the dark, Ash worked into his knuckle creases in the colour of the clean dark line, the pale clip-ring at his left wrist holding what light there is. \textbf{New on Day 171:} while Jorra’s bent finger stood in the cold iron and Sella’s sentence was allowed to finish, his broom checked half a beat behind the standing finger on the flagstones and went on without a word or a turn of the head; the shallow bright patch kept the place where the stroke stopped and neither man named the other’s silence. A third movement of the equality under the roof, the Seed 22 half-check returned changed, held and unspoken — not a reconciliation, a hearing, a stopping, a payment or a mercy, no payer named, no slate entered and the loan uncalled; the boy filed it on a place of its own beside the Day 161 fraction at the damper and the Day 166 held beat beneath the loaf shelf, three held changes on three places and not a pair, a doctrine or a rule (T036/T076, T062, T061/T082, T100). On Day 172 he told the kindling \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count} and brought the sentence about an ear under this roof being worth more than the debt that holds it to his teeth and no further; he drew the breath he should have spent, did not say the word that would call the loan, did not spend the Seed 16 breath and stood no tenth stopping before the seventh year was earned. Nine stoppings remained nine objects with no payer named to any, the loan stayed uncalled, and he went on believing something must give at the end of the seventh year though the end was not here. The warm stone Sella gave him in the winter Garl died lay cold in the clay pot in the loft, two years gone and unreconciled by not trying, which is not forgiving (T006 held). No new scar or possession, no change of voice, no bond paid or spoken.

His stroke went over the shallow bright patch on the flagstones without the half-check; the Day 171 movement stayed a held change on its own place beside the Day 161 damper fraction and the Day 166 held beat, not repeated as a new change and not paired into a rule with a payer. Seventh year nearer its end than it has ever stood and still held: six counted in the worn thumb-mark where the house can check and the seventh held at the lip where it cannot, the small knife at the very edge of its sill with Garl’s unforged collector sentence beside it, the Seed 16 breath unspent with its interval at the top of each reach, his chest tight since the dark, Ash worked into the knuckle creases in the colour of the clean dark line, the pale clip-ring at the left wrist holding what light there was. On all three days he told the kindling \emph{Six counted. The next I don’t count} and brought the ear-sentence to his teeth and no further: he drew the breath he should have spent, did not say the word that would call the loan, stood no tenth stopping up to join the nine because the seventh year has not yet been earned, and the loan stayed uncalled (T036/T076, T061/T082). His stroke went over the shallow bright patch on the flagstones without the half-check, so the Day 171 movement stayed a held change on its own place beside the Day 161 damper fraction and the Day 166 shelf beat, not repeated as a new change and not paired into a rule (T062, T100). \textbf{The chapter’s one meaningful change:} on the afternoon of Day 183 he went up into the Debt Loft and took the warm stone Sella gave him in the winter Garl died out of the unmarked clay pot where it had lain two years gone and cold, not looked at in a year; he held it, turned it so the light from the finger’s-width opening found the smooth place on one face, set it on the sill where a man coming up the ladder would see it, stood over it a long while and put it back, setting the pot’s foot down where it had stood. No word, no figure, no payer, no slate; he did not reconcile the stone with the debt and did not forgive it, for not trying is not forgiving, and the debt stands exactly as it stood. The stone lies back in the pot, cold and unreconciled, and on Days 184 and 185 he filed the remembering as a remembering and not a holding made again (T006 advanced, T036/T076 advanced, not paid). From below the boy heard only a small dry scrape of a pot’s foot on stone from a room he cannot enter, and kept it on a fourth place of its own (T061/T082). \chapter*{The Atlas}
\markboth{The Atlas}{The Atlas}
\addcontentsline{toc}{chapter}{The Atlas}
\CRmap*{The Cross and the Fishstairs — Sill’s market and the steps below the north bridge}{build/atlas/cross-and-fishstairs.jpg}{The ground the boy is carried over on every Account-day, drawn at the scale of the market: the market square with its stalls, the reading block under the moot-post and its finger’s width of shade, the eight pigs on the weighing rail and the turnips left standing with figures beside them, the Court’s table at the Slate Row fringe; below the north bridge the Fishstairs counting four steps, four, and the out-of-line landing, the edge of the fish-trade in the bridge’s shadow, Rusk’s room, the hard sill and the Singing Sill under the water, the dotted line of the Breaking, and the south bridge on the way to Low Kiln. Surveyed and inked in Y.H. 813, the reed month.}

\CRmap{Greybank, the Court’s gate}{build/atlas/greybank.jpg}{The Court’s granary town eighteen leagues downriver of Sill, drawn as its own surveyors would draw it: the Ilm and its quay, the factor’s house where the tally for Sill is kept, the Vhaleni Counting House with Veno Brine’s private drawer of dry documents, the Court’s granaries and banking hall, the winter ford, the burial grounds, and the ends of the Clay Road and the beginnings of the Salt and Hearth Roads. Surveyed and inked in Y.H. 812, the Thin Year.}

\CRmap*{High Kiln — the glaze terrace above Low Kiln, Sill}{build/atlas/high-kiln.jpg}{The other half of Sill, drawn at the scale a potter walks: the terrace two hundred paces above the low yard with its barley strip, House Clay and the folded red cord and locked box, the Glaze Room where lead is mixed and tasted, the master potters’ houses and their breathing kilns, the broken terrace lip, the steep street climbing from the north bridge and the Cross, the Ilm with its four-foot sill and Singing Sill, and Low Kiln below drawn faint for neighbourhood only. Surveyed and inked in Y.H. 812, the Thin Year.}

\CRmap*{Sill and the Lower Ilm — the country of the birth-town}{build/atlas/home-region.jpg}{The clay country about Sill, drawn out a few days’ walking: the Ilm from Nine Pots and the Ferr to Greybank, the weir, the Old Kiln, Cold Acre, Mud End and the Reedholt marsh. Surveyed and inked in Y.H. 812, the Thin Year.}

\CRmap{Sill and the Two Kilns — the birth-town}{build/atlas/home-settlement.jpg}{A detailed plan of Sill on the Ilm, drawn to the ground a child can walk: the four-foot fall and the Singing Sill, the two bridges, the Fishstairs and the Cross, Slate Row, Low Kiln with the Clay Yard and the Vail kiln-house, High Kiln and the Glaze Room, the family houses, the smithy, the meal mill, the wells and fields, the Bone Orchard and the edge of the reedbeds. Surveyed and inked in Y.H. 812, the Thin Year.}

\CRmap*{House Silt and the Birth Room — Low Kiln, Sill}{build/atlas/house-silt.jpg}{The house three doors down the Clay Yard from the Vail house, drawn at the scale at which a basket set just inside the door sees it: the front birth room with its bench by the door, hearth and slip pot, board-bed of grey wool with the hollow where the pale river stone lay, the round pewter tin above the bed with its pale fold and thumb-bright rub, the shelf’s chipped cup, the birth-slate and the six narrow pages turned face-down toward a floorboard, and the grey Ash ridge left where it lies along the skirting into the back room. There a neighbour scrubs at a board with lye water and a low song comes up through the floor. Around it, drawn faint: the Vail kiln-house, the smithy, the Drawing house, the drying racks, the slip pits, House Reed and the birth-flower shrine, the Slip Brook where Dessa Silt was taken, and the nineteen counted steps. Surveyed and inked in Y.H. 813, the month of Tallow.}

\CRmap{Keld Keep and the First Seam}{build/atlas/keld.jpg}{The Warden’s fortress city against the Rim and the deep survey cut into the stone beneath it, drawn cold and mineral as the Keep’s own survey-clerks would draw it: the walled Keep with the Warden’s hall and the mine-reeve’s room; the Rim Road coming up from Sill and going on ten leagues to the Cold Pass and its survey post; the Listening Stones five leagues higher in the Rim; and below, the timbered shaft of the First Seam with its galleries, the Descent, the Duelling Floor cut into the stone with nine clamps to the floor and the tenth behind the board, the survey room holding the crossed-out entry of Y.H. 588 and its branching red mark, the Ninth Gallery with the tin lined with warm-stone, a seam-serpent’s passing entered only as a change in the numbers, and the hot-lead warning of the Sweating. Cartouche dated Y.H. 812, the Thin Year, with a compass, a league scale, a convention of signs and surveyor’s notes on the measure before the name, the Warden’s claim, the once-a-year reading of the paper, and the insistence that no map is honest past the last pass.}

\CRmap*{Slate Row — the Court’s quarter in Sill}{build/atlas/slate-row.jpg}{The Court’s quarter, a quarter league east of the Cross, drawn at walking scale: the Clay Road passing through the Row to Greybank, the steep street climbing to High Kiln, the Ilm and its reedbeds along the south edge. The Court’s room with its bench by the door, pot, draught felt at the ankles and a place in the figures where a line should stand; the assessor’s narrow house of Y.H. 776; the collector’s table with its slate and cold-iron tube; the barred Waiting Room where the Forty of Low Kiln were held in Y.H. 812; the Court’s table at the market fringe and the printed one in twelve. Surveyed and inked in Y.H. 813, the month of Tallow.}

\CRmap*{The Clay Yard and the Vail House — Low Kiln, Sill}{build/atlas/the-clay-yard.jpg}{The close ground of Low Kiln drawn at the scale a clay child walks: the Clay Yard with its slip pits and ruts, the Vail kiln-house with its hearth, loaf shelf and bed, the wheel-shed with the Debt Loft and the finger’s-width-open back room, the drying racks with the space beneath the lowest, the row of houses to House Silt, the smithy, the well and the birth-flower shrine, the Slip Brook behind and the Ilm at the reedbeds. Surveyed and inked in Y.H. 812, the Thin Year.}

\CRmap{The Hearthseat on the Keel}{build/atlas/the-hearthseat.jpg}{The Court’s city, built over the Hearth a hundred and fifty leagues south-east of Sill, drawn cool and clean as its own surveyors would file it: the Weighing Hall with the grating of cold iron over the never-out fire and the Hearth shown in cut beneath the floor; Slate Row with the College of Assessors and its second file; the Steward’s room, the sealed files, the bank where measures are pressed into newborn vessels, the rooms of fewer than twenty Kept, the back rooms, the printed notice, the Hearth Road from Greybank and the way out to the Nine Wells. Surveyed and filed in Y.H. 812, the Thin Year.}

\CRmap*{The Old Kiln and the Ash Throat — one league south of Sill}{build/atlas/the-old-kiln.jpg}{The collapsed kiln in the grey clay a league south of Sill, drawn as its surveyor would draw it: the fallen crown and its broken brickwork, the fire mouth on the south-east flank, the flue broken at the top, the concentric throat where the ash runs deeper than a man, the hollow in its wall from which a slate was carried north to Low Kiln, the grey banks that will not take a glaze, the surveyor’s stakes and his cord, the track from Sill and the marsh way to Reedholt. A slow coil copied from the back of a slate is inked into the margin and left unread. Surveyed and inked in Y.H. 812, the Thin Year.}

\CRmap*{The Weir and the Eel Traps — one league upriver of Sill}{build/atlas/the-weir.jpg}{The eel weir on the Ilm a league upriver of Sill, drawn at the ground the trap-keepers walk: the V of stakes and its traps, the plank walk, Orra Weir’s hut and salting-racks, the hearth-maids’ blessing stone, the shoals and reeds, and the river road. Surveyed and inked in Y.H. 812, the Thin Year.}

\CRmap*{Vhal and the Sallow coast}{build/atlas/vhal.jpg}{A salt-chart of the principal Vhaleni port and the five leagues of shore east of it, drawn in the tar-and-wet-rope manner of the Council’s own surveyors: the Quay with its piers, crane, moored salt boats and the pulled benches; the Council room that smells of tar and wet rope, the tide-tally house and the glass furnaces within the town; the Salt Pans outside it with their dippers at dawn and their drying salt-paper; the blue-green Glaze Cliffs stained by old lead workings, and the glass-sand pits behind them; the silt-mouthed Ilm entering from the west and the Salt Road coming up from Greybank by the coast pass. In the sea the Sallow draw runs seaward against the wind, with a brine-gull, a salt boat and a salt-thing by report, and a surveyor’s notes on boat-shares passing through mothers, contracts that rot in the damp, and children warned not to lick the cliffs. Cartouche dated Y.H. 812, the Thin Year, with compass, league scale and a convention of signs.}

\CRmap*{Sarn — the bowl between Hearth and Waste}{build/atlas/world.jpg}{The known world as its own surveyors would draw it: the Rim and the cold beyond, the Sallow Sea, the Keel and the Hearth, and the nations between. Surveyed in Y.H. 812.}

\chapter*{The Reckoning of Days}
\markboth{The Reckoning of Days}{The Reckoning of Days}
\addcontentsline{toc}{chapter}{The Reckoning of Days}
\begin{CRtimeline}
\CRday{Day 170}{Tallow 21, Y.H. 813 (Firstday)  —  under the Vail kiln-house roof at the hearth and the bed, the kiln mouth, the drying racks, the yard well, the flagstones, the kindling and the loaf shelf, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath  —  The last working week opened with hot clay under tallow and the kiln breathing in fours with a gap while the carried fire under the floor answered four low pulls and missed its fifth, its payer unnamed for a hundred and seventy days, the boy one hundred and seventy days old and five months and twenty days and nobody under any roof saying so (T071/T072, T088); Sella Vail gave the instruction to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom and the running water and never to the basket, said the house where another woman would say I, kept her half-pace from every open slate and left the widow’s mark where it hung, for a morning and a shelf are not openings, and set the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand with her hand resting a half-beat longer than the setting needed (T058/T079); the yard went around the clean dark line, the finer grey called the thaw, the broken birth-slates beneath the lowest rack and the field’s empty place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out, with a look and a wide step and no number, the trough bare and dark with the water called weather and the clay jar cold under its glaze, glanced at once and not touched (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried); Tarn took the broom only after it had been instructed and told the kindling Six counted. The next I don’t count, with the small knife at the very edge of its sill and Garl’s unforged collector sentence beside it, six counted where the house could check and the seventh at the lip where it could not, his chest tight from the dark, Ash worked into his knuckles in the colour of the clean dark line and the pale clip-ring holding what light there was, his stroke going over the flagstones past the shallow bright patch and over the road a house sends a man down when it wants a collector without once turning along it and no collector coming, nine stoppings still nine with no tenth before the seventh year was earned and the Seed 16 breath unspent (T036/T076, T061/T082, T006 held); a pot set down wrong at the racks gave its high thin note before its time and the woman who set it down did not hear it, which he filed as a danger of the month and not as a fourth near-full answer, no room changed and no pot lost; a neighbour with a wet pot who asked what a firing cost set down there was sent to the pot with Ask the pot what a wet thing costs set down there. The house has said it, and carried the question away level, nothing slopped, nothing priced, nothing refused (T077); the charcoal under the loaf shelf waited unread and Sella’s finger did not go beneath the board, so the Day 161 fraction and the Day 166 held beat stood on separate places and did not stand up as a rule, three counts in three places and none becoming the others; at the going of the light she carried him home up the clay road, woodsmoke before her and river wind behind, going wide around the pan’s gone place, the bare dark trough and the space beneath the lowest rack without explaining the turns, set him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, put the fold right without looking at his face and left the thread of drool frozen and unwiped, and one hundred and seventy stood exact, complete and unspent in the dark of the wool, spoken by nobody under any roof.}
\CRday{Day 171}{Tallow 22, Y.H. 813 (Secondday)  —  the Vail wheel-shed, the cold damper, the flagstones, the finger’s-width-open back room (not entered), the drying racks, the yard well, the loaf shelf and the bed under the Vail kiln-house roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath  —  Before first grey three or four men came up the clay road with their collars high and went low into the back room, which kept its finger’s width of open, and Sella Vail carried past at the half-pace, turned no head, gave them no name and did not say the room was cold, while the boy did not count men who had been given no name and the two shut-room tellings stood side by side with no third (T035/T031, T065/T095); Jorra Vail came through with fine grey slate dust ground small as meal into both forearms past the bent little finger and under the nails, not bone-coloured slip, kept dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray, asked neither which slate had been broken nor whether it was a birth-slate, spoke to the wheel before anyone (It doesn’t care whose hands. It cares if they’re steady), told a pot You’ll do, knew its full note three turns before it left his hands and withheld the knowing from a High Kiln kiln-master who came up on the wrong wind and said a pot singing before its time generally sings itself out early, the knowing going to the near-full tray, beside the hearings and never among them, and no pot lost in the yard (T061/T082, T009/T013/T092); then came the chapter’s one meaningful change: when Sella’s voice went low with The fire’s low. It wants---, Jorra’s bent finger went to the cold iron of the damper and \textbf{held} while she finished It wants feeding, moved the tongue a hair’s breadth and left the finger standing in the iron, nobody speaking of the waiting and no payer named to the fraction, and while the finger still stood there Tarn, come up with the broom after it had been instructed, checked his stroke for half a beat behind the standing finger on the flagstones over the shallow bright patch kept since Seed 22, then went on toward the road without a word or a turn of the head, the stones keeping the patch where this stroke too had stopped (T062, T036/T076); the surgeon’s register measured the half-beat as the small distance between a hand’s intention and a hand’s arrest and left it in the margin, and the boy felt the thing before he understood it --- the Seed 22 half-check returned changed after a hundred and fifty days, in the very breath of a sentence allowed to finish and a finger standing in the iron, with both men looking elsewhere --- and filed it on a place of its own \textbf{beside} the Day 161 fraction at the damper and the Day 166 held beat beneath the loaf shelf, three held changes and not a pair, still less a doctrine, for a rule is an account that has found a payer and no payer stood to any of the three (T061/T082, T100 kept apart); at the well a neighbour’s question about what the firing would want now the kilns were hot was answered with the weather, the pot and the river and no figure, a man’s cold and a woman’s wet under it ended in weather, and Sella told the fire it was the thaw, turned the coals with the back of a broken pot, said The house will keep it, counted under her breath toward no opening and pushed coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak showed pale, while her finger stayed away from the loaf shelf and the charcoal waited unread (T077, T058/T079); in the small hours the file was laid out as instruments on a towel, six hearings beside and never among with no seventh and none invented, three near-full answers advanced and not paid with Jorra’s knowing among them, the older intervals at Stone 13, 17 and 25, and nine stoppings as objects and not a rule with no tenth before the seventh year was earned, the loan uncalled and the Seed 16 breath unspent; one hundred and seventy-one stood exact, complete and unspent in the dark of the wool, the fire missing its fifth with its payer unnamed for a hundred and seventy-one days and the river keeping its fifth low note through the door, three counts in three places and none becoming the others.}
\CRday{Day 172}{Tallow 23, Y.H. 813 (Thirdday)  —  the Clay Yard, the kiln mouth, the drying racks, the yard well, the kindling and flagstones, the clay road, and the Vail kiln-house hearth, loaf shelf and bed under the roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath  —  The last working week came into its third day with the kilns already at their heat and the yard smelling of a thing held at a temperature it would not stay at, the danger of the month in the dust ground small as meal, the sweetish edge of lead glaze riding up from High Kiln on a wrong wind and the kiln’s breath in fours with its gap, a wet pot giving its high thin note before its time which the boy filed as a danger and not as a fourth near-full answer, no room changed and no pot lost (T088, T061/T082); Tarn took the broom only after it had been given its instruction, set the small knife back at the very edge of its sill and told the kindling Six counted. The next I don’t count, six standing in the worn thumb-mark where the house could check and the seventh at the lip where it could not, Garl’s unforged collector sentence beside it, his chest tight from the dark, Ash worked into his knuckle creases in the colour of the clean dark line, the pale clip-ring at his left wrist holding what light there was, the warm stone she gave him in the winter Garl died lying cold in its clay pot in the loft, two years gone and not looked at in a year (T036/T076, T006 held); he said Yes, house to an early thaw and a late, agreeing so entirely that no argument could find a foot while going on wanting the late because a late thaw puts off the paying, his broom going over the collector’s road without once turning along it and no collector coming, and the sentence about an ear under this roof being worth more than the debt that held it came up into his teeth and went no further, the breath he should have spent drawn and not spent, the loan uncalled, no tenth stopping stood up before the seventh year was earned and something waiting to give at the end of a term that was not yet ended (T036/T076, T061/T082); at the well a woman’s question about what the kilns would want now the last week was in was answered with the heat kept, the pot and the river and no figure, and the yard went around the clean dark line, the finer grey called the thaw, the broken birth-slates and the field’s empty place with a look and a wide step and no number (T077, T009/T013/T092, T098 carried); Sella told the fire it was the thaw, turned the coals with the back of a broken pot, said The house will keep it, counted under her breath toward no opening, pushed coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist and set the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand without touching the widow’s mark, because a morning and a shelf are not openings (T058/T079); the surgeon’s register read the held breath as a clamp left too long and the near-saying stopped at the word as a chart closed over its finding with the neat margin showing, exact and worth nothing at two paces, an inventory that was not a key and a list that was not a hand; at the going of the light she carried him home up the clay road, woodsmoke before her and river wind behind, going wide around the pan’s gone place, the bare dark trough and the space beneath the rack, set him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, put the fold right without looking at his face, left the thread frozen and unwiped, let her hand rest a half-beat longer than the setting needed and went to her own bed, the two rooms not touching; in the small hours he laid out the file with six hearings and no seventh, three near-full answers advanced and not paid, nine stoppings with no payer named, the damper as one iron with two bites joined to no kiln, the two shut-room tellings with no third, the told bell beside the heard, and the third movement of the equality on Tallow 22 on a third place beside the Day 161 fraction and the Day 166 held beat --- three held changes and not a doctrine, no finger of his drawing the line between the shelf’s two gaps, the crust’s empty place, the pan’s gone ring and the field’s empty place, no third gap and no fourth likeness made a cause (T060/T086, T097, T062/T100); cold came cheek, temple, wrist and stopped, and one hundred and seventy-two stood exact, complete and unspent in the dark of the wool, the payer under the floor without a name for a hundred and seventy-two days, the charcoal waiting under the shelf for a hand that was not his and a day that had not come, as his hand outside the wool went up an inch toward the note of water over water and came down against the fold.}
\CRday{Day 173}{Tallow 24, Y.H. 813 (Fourthday)  —  under the Vail kiln-house roof at the hearth, the bed and the loaf shelf’s low angle, the kiln mouth, the drying racks, the yard well and the flagstones in the Clay Yard, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath  —  The last tend opened with hot clay under tallow and wet wool and the sour breath of the unswept corner beneath the sweet dry smell, the boy one hundred and seventy-three days old and five months and twenty-three days and nobody under any roof saying so (T071/T072), the kiln breathing behind the wall in fours with a gap while the carried fire under the floor answered four low pulls and missed its fifth with its payer unnamed for a hundred and seventy-three days (T088), the river’s note of water over water coming through the finger’s-width door as a fifth low thing never counted among the hearings and the boards keeping four nails, four, and a knot the width of a thumb, three counts in three places and none becoming the others (T061/T082); Sella Vail gave the instruction to the wool, the fire, the pot, the broom and the running water and never to the basket, said the house where another woman would say I, kept her half-pace, turned the coals with the back of a broken pot, told the fire it was the thaw, counted under her breath toward no opening, glanced once at the clay jar cold under its glaze without touching it, pushed coal-black hair back with the burn-wrist so the grey streak showed pale, set the pot rim out with its handle two inches beyond the reaching hand, let her hand rest a half-beat longer than the setting needed and left the widow’s mark untouched, for a morning and a shelf are not openings (T058/T079); the yard went around the clean dark line, the finer grey called the thaw, the broken birth-slates beneath the lowest rack, the pan’s gone ring and the field’s empty place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out, with a look and a wide step and no number (T009/T013/T092, T097/T098 carried), while a rack woman reached past the bare board with her hand before her eyes found the basket and two neighbours’ cold and wet-under-it ended in weather; Tarn took the broom only after it had been instructed, said Yes, house to an early thaw and a late while going on wanting the late because a late thaw puts off the paying, six counted in the worn thumb-mark where the house can check and the seventh at the lip where it cannot, Garl’s unforged collector sentence beside the knife, the ear-sentence up into his teeth and no further, the Seed 16 breath unspent, his stroke over the collector’s road without once turning along it and no collector coming, the half-check of Tallow 22 left where it was and not repeated (T036/T076, T061/T082); the month’s danger took its order in dust ground small as meal, the sweetish lead edge riding a wrong wind off High Kiln and a pot giving its thin note before its time, which the boy filed as a danger and not as a fourth near-full answer, no pot lost, no room changed, the firing read as a theatre he could not enter with heat kept and counted behind a screen and a gate of two bites, his file exact and worthless, an inventory that is not a key and a list that is not a hand, and one hundred and seventy-three standing exact, complete and unspent in the dark of the wool while the charcoal waited under the shelf for a hand that was not his and a day that had not come.}
\CRday{Day 174}{Tallow 25, Y.H. 813 (Fifthday)  —  the Vail wheel-shed, the cold damper, the flagstones, the drying racks and the yard well in the Clay Yard, the back room (not entered), the kiln-house hearth and the bed under the roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath  —  Before first grey three or four men came up with their collars high and went low through the finger’s-width door of the back room and Sella Vail carried past at the half-pace, turned no head, gave the house no name for them and did not say the room was cold, while the boy did not count men who had been given no name and the two tellings of a counting room shut in the war stood side by side with no third (T035/T031, T065/T095); Jorra Vail came through with fine grey slate dust ground small as meal into both forearms past the bent little finger and under the nails, white in the creases where a fist had opened and not bone-coloured slip, kept dusty forearms and clean ones on one tray and asked neither which slate had been broken nor whether it was a birth-slate, the broken birth-slates lying under the lowest rack and entered by nobody; he spoke to the wheel before anyone (It doesn’t care whose hands. It cares if they’re steady), told a pot You’ll do, knew the full note it would give three turns before it left his hands and withheld the knowing from a High Kiln kiln-master come up on the wrong wind who said a pot singing before its time generally sings itself out early, the knowing going to the near-full tray, beside the hearings and never among them, advanced and not paid, no pot lost and no lesson made (T061/T082); when Sella’s voice went low at the hearth with The fire’s low. It wants---, Jorra’s bent finger went into the cold iron of the damper and \textbf{held} there while she finished feeding and gave the end of the instruction to the pot, then moved the tongue a hair’s breadth and left the finger standing, nobody speaking of the waiting and no payer named to the fraction, the holding remembered and not a word and its coming round again not a change twice over (T062); Tarn’s stroke went over the shallow bright patch on the flagstones without the half-check and over the collector’s road without once turning along it, neither man looking toward the other or naming the other’s silence, and the three held changes --- the Day 161 damper fraction, the Day 166 beat beneath the loaf shelf and the Tallow 22 flagstone half-check --- stayed three on three places and did not stand up as a rule, for a rule is an account that has found a payer; at the well a woman’s question about what the kilns would want now the last tend was in was answered with the weather, the pot and the river and never a figure, sent to the pot with Ask the pot what a wet thing costs set down there. The house has said it, carried away level so nothing slopped, nothing was priced and nothing refused (T077), and the widow’s mark hung where it hung, for a well and a morning are not openings (T058/T079); under the floor the carried fire missed its fifth with its payer unnamed for a hundred and seventy-four days and the river kept its fifth low thing through the door, and one hundred and seventy-four stood exact, complete and unspent, told by nobody, the boy having stopped expecting to be told, which was not the same as not wanting it.}
\CRday{Day 175}{Tallow 26, Y.H. 813 (Sixthday)  —  the yard well, the drying racks, the worked strips, the loaf shelf and hearth under the Vail kiln-house roof, the clay road at the going of the light and the bed under the roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath  —  Midday stood in the Clay Yard with the heat held in the clay and the oiled paper lifting at the kiln-house windows, Sella Vail carrying the boy at the half-pace with instruction to the wool, the running water and the river wind and never to the basket, and a neighbour with a pot just out of the tubs asking what a firing cost set down in the Vail house being answered, after one glance at the cold glazed jar and a hand that shut half over nothing without touching it, with Ask the pot what a wet thing costs set down there. The house has said it, the question going away level in the arm that carried it, nothing slopped, nothing priced, nothing refused, an answer given as a direction that arrived nowhere and left no entry (T077, T058/T079); two neighbours settled the morning between a cold and a wet one under it and the argument ended in weather with nobody owning either day, while the yard went around the clean dark line, the finer grey called the thaw, the space beneath the lowest rack where the broken birth-slates lay and the empty place where a hand went in on Seed 15 and did not come out, with a look and a wide step and no number, dry slip dust fine as meal in the creases of a fist and the sweetish lead edge off High Kiln coming and going on a wrong wind, entered in nothing (T009/T013/T092, T098 carried); under the roof the underside of the loaf shelf became a roof over the basket and Sella stood with her back to it, moving her lips along her row with two unnamed gaps, giving nobody a figure, while a rack woman put two bare boards and a child’s appetite under one appetite in one breath and the boy kept the shelf’s two gaps, the fold’s crust and its empty place, the pan’s gone ring on its own tray and the field’s empty place in four rooms and on four trays that did not touch, no third gap coming, no fourth likeness made a cause and no finger of his drawing the line (T060/T086, T097); the charcoal waited under the shelf’s front edge unread and uncounted, her finger not going beneath the board, so the Day 166 held beat stood where it had been left, and the boy did not read, count or copy the marks, which waited for a hand that was not his and a day that had not come (T100 carried, not paid); at the going of the light she carried him home up the clay road, woodsmoke before her and river wind behind, going wide around the pan’s gone place, the bare dark trough, the rack space and the missing hand’s place without explaining the turns, and under the roof set him on his bed and not in the Debt Loft, put the fold right without looking at his face, left the thread frozen, let her hand rest a half-beat longer, told the fire it was the thaw, said The house will keep it, counted under her breath toward no opening, set the pot handle two inches beyond the reaching hand and left the widow’s mark untouched, because a dusk is not an opening and the two rooms do not touch; the cold arriving cheek, temple and wrist stopped at the wrist with the afterdrop waiting, and one hundred and seventy-five stood exact, complete and unspent while the fire missed its fifth with its payer unnamed for a hundred and seventy-five days.}
\CRday{Day 176}{Tallow 27, Y.H. 813 (Seventhday)  —  the Clay Yard and the kiln mouth, the drying racks, the yard well, the kindling and flagstones under the Vail roof, the loaf shelf and the bed under the roof, Low Kiln, Sill, Grath  —  The last tend stood at its heat with the yard smelling of a thing held between two hands that would not stay held, the danger of the month in dust ground small as meal on the sill and white in the whites of knuckles, the sweetish edge of lead glaze riding a wrong wind off High Kiln and the kiln’s breath in fours with its gap, an order and no name that could not be carried into a chart, a rack woman’s pot giving its thin early sound filed where a danger goes and not among the three near-full answers or the six hearings, no pot lost and no room changed (T061/T082);
